reason: XCTExpectFailure now gets its own 'Expected Failure' status bucket instead of folding into passed (docs/release-notes/4.0.0.md, 'The Xcode-native report redesign': 'All six outcomes get a bucket' / 'Expected failures have a filter pill (#460)'). This harness reads 2.5.1/3.0.0 rows from their -j JUnit export (README), which has no expected-failure state and has reported it as `unknown`/passed since long before the distinction existed (Sources/XCTestHTMLReportCore/Classes/Models/JUnitReport.swift, TestCase init comment) -- a JUnit-source limitation, not new information withheld by the report.

A test that fails then passes on retry now reports the dedicated 'Mixed' status (docs/release-notes/4.0.0.md: the filter pills include 'a permanent Mixed (0)' bucket). Verified 3.0.0's own rendered HTML report (render/3.0.0/RetryResults/index.html) also shows 'Mixed' for this test -- the divergence here is that this harness reads old-lineage rows from JUnit XML (README), which cannot express a mixed/retried outcome and always reports the run's last iteration; not a regression in what either report actually shows.

Same Expected-Failure bucket change as RetryTests/testInUnknownState() -- see docs/release-notes/4.0.0.md 'All six outcomes get a bucket' / 'Expected failures have a filter pill (#460)'; JUnit (the old-lineage source here) has no expected-failure state (JUnitReport.swift TestCase init comment).

Swift Testing's withKnownIssue is the Swift Testing counterpart to XCTExpectFailure and gets the same new 'Expected Failure' status bucket -- see docs/release-notes/4.0.0.md 'All six outcomes get a bucket' / 'Expected failures have a filter pill (#460)'; JUnit (the old-lineage source here) has no expected-failure state (JUnitReport.swift TestCase init comment).

The old lineage's JUnit fabricated a synthetic 'System Failures' TEST row and rendered it green/passed, counted in the totals as an ordinary success -- actively misleading about a run whose host app trapped at launch. 4.0's report.json models the same bucket as an empty GROUP (no test-case children) per #478's 'a run that stopped early is now a fault, not a clean exit' (docs/release-notes/4.0.0.md), so it legitimately has no row for a row-based comparison to find; this mask covers that deliberate removal, not a loss. #478's 'a run that stopped early is now a fault' does not yet reach the rendered HTML: neither rc1 nor HEAD shows any fault indication (the group renders as succeeded), and shipped 4.0.0rc1's CLI exits 0; HEAD exits non-zero with a stderr warning. That open product gap is tracked separately by the maintainers.
